newsitem.title: MEXICO: Final election results in Mexico's Guerrero state.
newsitem.headline: Final election results in Mexico's Guerrero state.

text.p: The left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) emerged as the big gainer in Guerrero state elections on October 6, according to final results from the state electoral commission released at the weekend.
The PRD won 19 of the state's 76 town halls, including the third biggest city, Iguala -- 13 more than in the last such elections in 1993.

The ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) won 54 town halls, down from 68 last time. It managed to cling on to Guerrero's biggest city Acapulco by a slim margin over the PRD but won the second city and state capital of Chilpancingo comfortably.

The conservative National Action Party (PAN) won its first town hall in the state, the colonial-era silver town of Taxco, and the hard-left Workers Revolutionary Party (PRT) held onto two mayoralties.
In elections for the 46-person state congress, the PRI won 30 deputies, the PRD 12, the PAN two and the PRT one. The remaining seat was won by the tiny left-wing Cardenist Party.
